summary: Linked-list destructor for a container at this. Optionally closes the handle stored at this+0x10 (gated by the byte flag at this+0x18, and only cleared on CloseHandle success), then walks the node list from the head at this+0x0. For each node, when the byte flag at node+0x8 is set and the node's data pointer at node+0x0 is non-null, invokes the second vtable destructor (vtable+0x4) on the data object as a __thiscall with argument 1, then frees the node wrapper with FreeWrapper_7bcf. Finally zeroes the list head, tail, cursor and element count.

operations.description: Guard on byte flag at this+0x18; when set, close the handle stored at this+0x10 via CloseHandle.
CloseHandle must report success for the handle field to be cleared.
Clear the handle field at this+0x10 to 0 after a successful CloseHandle.
Walk the linked list from the head pointer at this+0x0, following each node's next-link (node+0x4) until null.
Per node: if the byte flag at node+0x8 is set and the node's data pointer at node+0x0 is non-null, invoke the vtable destructor.
Invoke the second vtable destructor (entry at vtable+0x4) on the node's data object as a __thiscall with argument 1.
Free the node wrapper via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Zero the list head pointer at this+0x0 after destruction.
Zero the list tail pointer at this+0x4 after destruction.
Zero the cursor/iterator pointer at this+0x8 after destruction.
Zero the element count at this+0xC after destruction.
Void return: the list is fully destroyed and all container fields are cleared.

unresolved: Exact node structure (data pointer, byte flag, next-link layout) and the identity of the released data object type are inferred from layout only.
Whether the vtable+0x4 destructor called with argument 1 is the primary or a secondary destructor of the data object is unresolved.
